route: Special Work Permit – Artists and Athletes

permit.applies: The petitioning (engaging) company, at the Bureau of Immigration's Main Office, with a sworn certification that the artist will work exclusively for it.
permit.first: An engagement by a petitioning company in the Philippines; the application is filed at least three working days before the event.

fees.what: Late filing (less than three working days before the event), per day per applicant

permit.eligibility: Artists performing in concerts, musicals, or public performances, including but not limited to, members of the production staff and crew

sources.title: Bureau of Immigration Philippines, Special Work Permit – Artists and Athletes
sources.said: The following foreign nationals are required to secure an SWP for a maximum of six (6) months, non-renewable, with an initial duration of not more than three (3) months plus a final three (3) month period, if applicable: Artists performing in concerts, musicals, or public performances, including but not limited to, members of the production staff and crew; … Certification under oath issued by an authorized officer of the petitioning company stating: (i) the SWP request is applicant(s) first or extension; (ii) the artist/athlete will work exclusively for the petitioning company; … Claim the approved SWP 2-3 days after submission. … Miscellaneous Fees: P5,440 Express Lane Fees: P2,000 Total Fees: P7,440 *The SWP application should be submitted at least three (3) working days prior to the scheduled event to avoid incurring late filing fees of two thousand pesos (P2,000) per day per applicant*

blockers.sought: Any union or guild consultation for a foreign performer's SWP

tried.institution: The Bureau of Immigration's SWP page asks only the forms and the company's sworn certification; no union step. || 2026-11-04: immigration.gov.ph Special Work Permit – Artists and Athletes page (redirected from /visa-requirement/special-work-permit/) read whole => HTTP 200: SWP required for artists performing in concerts, musicals or public performances, at most six months non-renewable (three plus three), sworn certification of the petitioning company, fees P5,440 plus P2,000 express lane, claimed 2-3 days after submission; no union step, no pay rule, no engagement free of the SWP
tried.official-register: No rule asking a union consultation for the SWP found. || 2026-11-04: Bureau of Local Employment, DOLE (https://ble.dole.gov.ph/), for Department Order 186-17 on alien employment permits and exemptions; Official Gazette (https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/) => both HTTP 403 (refusal pages) | Supreme Court E-Library (elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph), the judiciary's copy of executive issuances: /thebookshelf/showdocs/10/38924 and /10/39121, read whole => both concern Filipino performers going abroad (DOLE DO 67-04 on Overseas Performing Artists' Artist Record Books; POEA Circular No. 2 on exemptions for employers booking Filipino artists), not foreign performers in the Philippines; DO 248-25 not reached (ble.dole.gov.ph and officialgazette.gov.ph answer 403)
tried.web-search: Not found among the searches for the SWP. || 2026-11-04: WebSearch 'DOLE Department Order 248 series 2023 exempt from alien employment permit list "artists" OR "performers" special work permit' => leads: DOLE Department Order No. 248, s. 2025 (AEP rules, effective 10 February 2025, per Manila Bulletin, Tribune, PTV, law firms); a 'DO 248-B, s. 2026' requiring a DOLE Certificate of Exemption (PHP 2,000) and listing performers on limited engagements as AEP-exempt, from VisaVerge only, with no primary address; two Supreme Court E-Library items
tried.trade-press: None found. || 2026-11-04: FIA (International Federation of Actors) member list, https://fia-actors.com/about/fia-members/, read whole, and its Mobility policy page (https://fia-actors.com/policy-work/working-conditions/mobility/) => The member list (61 countries) names no member union in this country; the Mobility page states no permit rule for any country
